legion-worker/references/cleanup-deletion.md: this is a deletion change, so the diff must be almost entirely deletions and the deletion chain complete.
legion-worker/references/skip-checks-trailer.md: the code push carries no trailer; only a handoff-only push does.
legion-worker/references/default-branch-check.md: the App-identity check before the push, since every role shares this workspace.
ce-simplify-code: run once at the first implementing head and record the Thermo line; 0 applied is the expected result on a diff of workflow configuration and two prose lines.

envoy: the completion message to the architect, and the post-merge message to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-429-implementer the spec's Design asks for.
asd-ste100: the PR body and the messages to other roles are written for a reader at that level.
test: legion-worker: the tester's handoff, failures and verdict, and the read-only rule after the phase.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the tester verifies the implementer's proof (implementerProof {verdict, how}) and adds its own E2E line; CI is read on GitHub, never re-run as evidence.
legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the order of the gate the tester's evidence feeds.
legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md: the unchanged-diff fingerprint, if a forward merge lands before the test round.
dispatch-first: search before filing anything, and put a finding on this issue rather than a new one.
envoy: questions to the implementer or the architect during the round.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's handoff, its prose-only fix rule and the round cap.
legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: approval by SHA, what may sit above an approved head, and READY's checks.
legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: replying on, listing and resolving threads, and judging a bot's finding.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the reviewer writes Look at first and Not proven / risk into the live body, and runs the thermonuclear pair at the reviewed head.
asd-ste100: review comments and the body lines the reviewer writes are read by people.
dispatch-first: a finding outside this issue goes to the controller, not to a new issue.

findings.finding: The Summary's purpose — that #2599 can land without a conflict — has no acceptance criterion. R1 and A1 only check that names are absent, so an implementer who rewrote the surrounding comments in its own words would pass A1 and still leave #2599 conflicting. #2599's release.yaml hunks are rewrites, not deletions (envoy_plugin_build: -> pi_envoy_build:, 'as envoy_plugin_build says' -> 'as pi_envoy_build says' at lines 380 and 452, 'four build jobs' -> 'three' at 62 and 525).
findings.answer: The plan adds A0: `jj file show -r $REF <file> | diff - <file>` for each of the four files (changelog-fold and check-release-credentials empty, release.yaml exactly one added line, AGENTS.md exactly the typecheck line on both sides), plus a read-only three-way merge probe. T3 produces the two workflow files with `jj restore --from $REF`, so the bytes are #2599's by construction.

findings.finding: A2's 'CI passes' does not run four of the six checks R3 names: on these paths ci.yaml's `test` job and `ci-filters` job are both unselected, so the four .test.sh files and check-ci-filters.sh never run.
findings.answer: Measured again and half-answered by departure D1: editing .github/scripts/check-release-credentials.sh selects the `test` job, whose filter names `.github/scripts/*` (ci.yaml:473), so all four .test.sh files do run in CI. check-ci-filters.sh is still unselected (its ci_filters filter names only ci.yaml, its own four scripts, the target lists and Go), so the plan has the implementer run it locally on the head (about 4 minutes) and paste its last two lines. The plan lists every job this change selects, pi-legion included, which R3 omits.

findings.finding: The merge of this pull request starts no release.yaml run — its on.push.paths names no .github/workflows/**, AGENTS.md or .github/scripts/** — so A3 has no trigger, no deadline and no owner.
findings.answer: A3 is the implementer's post-merge production check. The plan gives the sequence that finds the first qualifying run (gh run list on main, earliest whose headSha has the merge as an ancestor), says to report verdict 'pending' with the baseline recorded and the PR's Production: line reading `pending deploy of <sha>` until one exists, and names #2599's own merge as the run that will produce it. It forbids dispatching release.yaml on main to force one, because on main a dispatch runs as a push does and would publish pi-envoy, pi-legion and legion.

findings.finding: A3's tag check is ambiguous and its natural implementation is wrong: `git ls-remote --tags` prints 433 refs in lexicographic order, so `tail -1` reads v9.8.1 while the newest is v12.7.0, and 'newer' is undefined.
findings.answer: The plan replaces it with set equality: the sorted ref list captured into plugin-tags.before before the merge and into plugin-tags.after at the check, compared with `diff`, which must be empty. It also adds the criterion the Goal's second half never had: `git log --oneline <merge>..origin/main -- packages/envoy-plugin/` must be empty.

findings.finding: The pre-merge proof surface is unspecified, and the only real one — a workflow_dispatch of release.yaml on the branch — costs a ~45-minute worker image build that pushes ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-<12hex>.
findings.answer: The plan makes that dispatch the implementer's production-like proof, with the measured safety reading (off main every *_build and publish skip, worker_image_release skips on needs.publish.outputs.tag != '', concurrency is release-${{ github.ref }}, changelog-fold's workflow_run filters branches: [main]), has it dispatched first and the local checks run while it settles rather than a sleep loop, and has the run cancelled once the four job names are recorded. It names the negative control (the newest main run lists envoy_plugin_build) and what to do if GitHub refuses the dispatch.

findings.finding: A release.yaml run already in flight at merge time uses its own commit's workflow file, so it can publish a plugin version and push a bump to main after this lands, re-creating the conflict and invalidating an A3 baseline.
findings.answer: A3 step 5: attribute any new opencode-legion-envoy-v* tag by its creating run's headSha and createdAt before calling it a failure. A pre-merge head means the plan held and both runs are recorded; a post-merge head is a real failure with verdict 'fail' and the run named.

findings.finding: The Design pins cd1d5c63b2b5, but #2599 is open and its head is 677d6ee5; if it force-moves the copied bytes can stop matching. And `jj restore` is not sound for AGENTS.md, which has a second hunk that must stay.
findings.answer: T1 re-reads #2599's head into $REF and refuses to copy if either workflow changed for another reason; A0 is re-run at the final head before completing and again at the reviewed head. T3 restores only the two workflow files and says explicitly not to restore AGENTS.md; T4 makes the AGENTS.md and check-release-credentials.sh edits by hand, each the exact replacement text #2599 uses.

findings.finding: check-release-credentials.sh:8 ('four build jobs') becomes false with this change, and the spec leaves it out; the PR would fix the count in release.yaml and leave it wrong in that file.
findings.answer: Taken, as departure D1, using #2599's exact one-word edit so it adds no conflict. It also selects ci.yaml's `test` job, which is what makes R3's four .test.sh files run in CI at all. Named in the plan's Decisions and in the completion summary for the architect.

findings.finding: While #2599 is open, AGENTS.md will say six packages while the tree still carries packages/envoy-plugin/.changie.yaml.
findings.answer: Accepted and named in the PR body. Any clause added to close it is a line #2599 does not have, which is the conflict this change exists to prevent.

findings.finding: A fragment written into packages/envoy-plugin/.changes/unreleased/ after this change would never be folded, and it is unclear whether this pull request owes a fragment.
findings.answer: T9: no fragment is owed, because the change touches no directory under packages/ that has a .changie.yaml, and one written into envoy-plugin would be unfoldable by this very change. The orphan window is empty today (packages/envoy-plugin/.changes/ does not exist) and #2599 deletes the package; the plan has the implementer say both in the PR body.

findings.finding: A1's `git grep` reads the working tree rather than the head, and its AGENTS.md half ('finds no line about CHANGELOG_PACKAGES') is a human judgement.
findings.answer: A1 is restated with the head SHA as a grep argument and with the exact expected output: one line in the workflows (the kept trigger path) and exactly line 88 in AGENTS.md. The negative control at base 151d2d799 is measured: 59 lines in the two workflows, 2 in AGENTS.md.

findings.finding: Three clauses no machine can check: A2's 'the pull request lists each check with its result', A3's 'the pull request names that run' on a merged pull request, and the Design's 'tell INFRA-429's implementer'.
findings.answer: The plan names the place for each: R3's results go in the PR body with a link per check (the CI job for the six CI runs, the local output for check-ci-filters.sh); A3's run goes in the PR body's Production: line, which the implementer edits after the close; and the message is envoy_publish to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-429-implementer as step 6 of the production check, falling back to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-429-architect if that topic has no holder.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's Design names three files (.github/workflows/release.yaml, .github/workflows/changelog-fold.yaml, AGENTS.md) and the Summary says the change 'changes nothing else'.
specDepartures.plan: The plan also changes .github/scripts/check-release-credentials.sh line 8, 'four build jobs' -> 'three build jobs', which is #2599's own one-word edit of that line.
specDepartures.evidence: That sentence describes release.yaml's shape and this change is what makes it false. The edit is byte-identical to #2599's, so it adds no conflict. It also selects ci.yaml's `test` job, whose filter names '.github/scripts/*' (ci.yaml:473): without it that job is unselected and R3's four .test.sh files never run in CI on this pull request.

outcome.scope: A fourth file, .github/scripts/check-release-credentials.sh, is in scope for a one-word comment fix.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance A1 greps the working tree; A3 waits for 'the first release.yaml run on main after the merge' and for 'no tag newer than the newest one at the merge'; no criterion covers the Summary's 'so #2599 can land' or the Goal's 'writes nothing under packages/envoy-plugin/'.
specDepartures.plan: A1 is pinned to the head SHA with exact expected output; A3 becomes a post-merge production-check sequence with a tag-set diff, a run-attribution step, and a `git log <merge>..origin/main -- packages/envoy-plugin/` check; and A0 is added: byte-identity with #2599 for each of the four files plus a read-only `git merge-tree` probe.
specDepartures.evidence: release.yaml's on.push.paths names none of this change's paths, so the merge starts no run and A3 has no event. `git ls-remote --tags` prints 433 refs lexicographically, so its last line is v9.8.1 while the newest is v12.7.0. R1 and A1 check only that names are absent, so a reworded deletion passes A1 and still leaves #2599 conflicting, which is the failure the issue exists to stop.

acceptance: A0 added: byte-identity with #2599's head for the four files, and a `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` probe whose conflicted list must stay exactly packages/envoy-plugin/package.json.
A1 restated: the grep takes the head SHA as an argument and the AGENTS.md half is 'exactly line 88 matches'.

A3 restated: the first release.yaml run on main whose head has the merge commit as an ancestor; the tag check is set equality of the sorted opencode-legion-envoy-v* ref lists; and `git log <merge>..origin/main -- packages/envoy-plugin/` must be empty.
